newsitem.title: USA: Iceland's magnesium plant study positive so far.
newsitem.headline: Iceland's magnesium plant study positive so far.

text.p: A feasibility study for building a 50,000-tonne-per-year primary magnesium plant in Iceland is due to be completed next month and the outcome looks positive, officials linked to the project said.
"We have not found anything yet to say it's not a viable project," said Julius Jonsson of Icelandic Magnesium Project. He added the feasibility study will be completed late in February.

IMP has already formed a joint venture, Icelandic Magnesium Corp, with Germany's Salzgitter Anlagenbau GmBH, part Preussag AG, and Consortium Magniy, a grouping of companies from the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
The energy-intensive project would benefit from cheap power generated by geothermal steam.
Columbia Ventures of the U.S. is also considering reassembling a German aluminum smelter in Iceland because of the cheap power.
The new magnesium plant would represent a sizeable addition to annual world production which currently totals about 260,000 tonnes.
Primary magnesium is used to make alloyed magnesium for diecast automotive parts, the metal's brightest growth prospect.
